rationale: C25 is a closely preceding amendment to an executive order establishing a military service medal. It supplies the same concrete drafting machinery: replace provisions of an existing medal order with eligibility language defining covered members, qualifying service, administrative regulations, and interservice treatment. C18 is also a substantial medal-eligibility directive, but it is a freestanding Purple Heart order rather than an amendment to an existing medal order. C06 provides amendment-and-replacement structure but concerns hospitalization and lacks the award machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Armed Forces Reserve Medal may be awarded to members or former members of the reserve components of the armed forces of the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby established the Korean Service Medal ... for award ... to members of the armed forces of the United States
shared_material.explanation: Both formulate eligibility for a named military medal by identifying covered members of the armed forces.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Including the Coast Guard Reserve and the Marine Corps Reserve ... Including annual active-duty and Inactive-duty training as required by appropriate regulations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: for award, under such regulations as the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force and the Secretary of the Treasury may severally prescribe, and subject to the provisions of this order
shared_material.explanation: Both place detailed medal eligibility within an interservice regulatory framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Provided (1) that such ten years of service is, or has been, performed within a period of twelve consecutive years ... And provided further
